First, finding headroom reports that the crown is outside the picture on 76% of frames — only 24% of frames have the crown visible, well below the 50% minimum required by the crown_visible gate. Rows that were never recorded cannot be reconstructed; fix.reframe can reposition and scale existing pixels but cannot invent a crown that the camera never captured. This means the crown_visible gate (≥ 0.5) will fail verification regardless of any fix or process applied. Additionally, finding picture_area shows the recorded picture is only 1620×1080 inside a 1920×1080 file (pillarboxed), compounding the framing issues. With the crown_visible gate structurally unpassable (only 0.24 recorded vs 0.50 required), and no allowed strategy addressing it, the honest exit is reshoot. Sandy should: (1) export without padding — send the 1620-wide picture without pillarboxing, per reshoot_guidance picture_area; (2) stand 2–3 m from the camera and frame head to mid-thigh before the take starts — do not walk toward the camera, per reshoot_guidance subject_size and distance_steady; (3) leave 5–12% of the frame height above the hair crown at all times, per reshoot_guidance crown_visible.
